headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Dify’s broad egress and filesystem access can amplify any content from the non-runnable awesome-nlp list into external actions or outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is a non-runnable open-source list with no shared channel to Dify, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or user-supplied content into Dify workflows, which makes hijack possible but unusual. Dify’s agent/workflow tool wiring and file inputs increase exposure if such content is imported.
conditions: IF a user copies content from awesome-nlp into a Dify prompt or knowledge file
IF Dify treats imported text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Require explicit instruction/data delimiters in prompts
Strip or neutralize markdown and code fences before ingestion
Review imported content before attaching it to workflows
Use a separate staging workspace for pasted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify reads filesystem uploads and sends content to model providers and user-defined OpenAPI tools, while awesome-nlp is a public repository/list that could be pasted or uploaded into those flows. The pair does not show a shared OS workspace, but Dify’s broad egress means any sensitive material introduced through the list or adjacent files can leave the environment by default.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is uploaded into Dify knowledge files
IF Dify routes that content to a model provider or OpenAPI tool
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive files into Dify
Disable unnecessary OpenAPI tools
Use a redaction pass before ingestion
Restrict model-provider access to approved tenants

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp itself has no write or execution surface, but Dify can execute shell code server-side and write files, creating overlap if the list is used as a source for generated artifacts or workflows. The interaction is not a direct same-directory conflict, yet Dify’s write and subprocess capabilities make concurrent mutation or unintended artifact creation plausible once user content is imported.
conditions: IF Dify workflows write artifacts derived from awesome-nlp content
IF multiple Dify instances share the same datastore or output directory
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per workflow
Disable shell steps unless required
Add a manual review step before writes
Use per-run unique filenames

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a curated list, so Dify may treat its entries as authoritative source material when building prompts, RAG content, or workflow steps. Dify’s agent/orchestrate features can then act on that output via tools or model providers without a built-in verification step shown here, making misclassification or stale recommendations propagate downstream.
conditions: IF Dify ingests awesome-nlp entries as facts or recommendations
IF downstream tools act on those generated outputs without human review
mitigations: Add citation checks before tool execution
Require human approval for tool-triggering outputs
Tag imported list items as untrusted reference material
Log source provenance alongside generated actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU residency, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, while Dify explicitly stores conversation logs and knowledge-base content. The only concrete compliance concern is that Dify may retain imported content longer than the source list implies, but the pair does not evidence a regulated-data transfer or residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Dify knowledge files or conversation logs
IF retention settings are left at defaults for that regulated data
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Dify
Set short retention windows
Purge conversation logs after use
Document data-class handling rules
